target_customer: Individuals, creators and small teams tired of email and Slack
problem: Email and chat tools are noisy and distracting; Memo offered asynchronous messages meant to be high value.
business_model: Free during validation; subscription not established

founders.name: Richard Shepherd
previous_startups: Creative agency in south west England (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: UK full-stack web developer with sales experience; later founded DID.app.

founders.name: Peter Saxton
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page: developer in API design, UI and infrastructure reliability, physics background including quantum optics; later founded DID.app.

competitors.name: Hey (Basecamp)
competitors.what: Paid email service that screens senders and groups threads

competitors.name: Superhuman
competitors.traction_then: Described as a paid email service in June 2020 coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: A messaging web app with magic link sign in; standard engineering for two developers.

defensibility.rationale: Messaging apps are easy to copy and a new network had to be seeded from zero.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Basecamp shipped Hey in June 2020. No source shows an incumbent copying Memo.

market_need_then: Complaints about email and Slack overload were widespread in 2020, shown by the launch of Hey and press about improving email (Axios, June 2020).

branding.domain_note: Used sendmemo.app, a suffix and .app domain

identity.voice_and_tone: Anti attention economy pitch: 'mad as hell about their time being sold to the highest bidder'

branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt on 2021-03-25 per an Indie Hackers post; no wider community found

brand_strength.rationale: The name Memo is generic and shared by many products; search returns many unrelated Memo companies.

outcome_analysis: Memo was a two developer team in YC Summer 2020 building an alternative to email and Slack, launched on Product Hunt in March 2021 as a free product, and is now Inactive with both founders working on DID.app. The cause of closure is not public. A new messaging network with no moat and a generic name faced strong rivals such as Hey, Superhuman and Slack, so distribution was likely the hard part, but that is inference rather than a stated reason.
notes: Company site sendmemo.app returned HTTP 522 so its state is unknown. Cause of inactive status not public. CB Insights shows a 0.5 million convertible note dated 2020-01-01 from Y Combinator for a Memo entry, but its description (digital tools for online presence) does not match this company and the date precedes the batch, so it is not recorded as a round. The same figure and date appear on other YC entries and look like a database default. Other Memo companies (fundraising memos, Signal AI) are unrelated.
